correctness.rationale: For fixed positive a,b and an interior target, each positive second phase ζ≤a+bπ uniquely determines the segment y=(ζ-ax)/(bπ), on x in (0,1] intersected with [(ζ-bπ)/a,ζ/a]. On it the first phase divided by π is a/x+ζ/π²−ax/π², strictly decreasing. Each of the two distinct first-phase progressions crosses it at most once per integer, equivalently at the unique positive quadratic root. The inverse labels are injective because the actual phases fix both labels. Exactly the phases 0<ζ≤bπ have segments reaching x=0, including equality where y=1−ax/(bπ). Their two disjoint second-phase progressions give the stated floors. Counting integers on each truncated phase interval gives a/ε+O(1) per first-phase progression on an edge-reaching segment and a bounded count elsewhere. The smallest phase is arcsin(sqrt(v)), giving the if-and-only-if threshold, including equality when b<1/2. The phase Jacobian determinant is −ab(1+π²/x²), and the two sine derivatives are nonzero at interior targets. For K>0, each edge-reaching segment has weight 1/K+O(ε); its transverse distance to ζ/(bπ) is ax/(bπ), with x=a/m+O(m⁻²). Summing the distances gives a harmonic logarithm, while exceptional segments and weight rebalancing cost O(ε). This proves the stated W1 upper bound without uniformity near target endpoints or staircase jumps.
